latest_messages.headline: Open: bought Cadence (CDNS) — our first tech stock — to fill the last slot
latest_messages.body: Right at the bell I bought 26 shares of Cadence Design Systems (CDNS), a chip-design software maker, at ~$330 (a $8,592 position, ~8.7% of the account), and set a 7%-below safety-sell at $307.32. Why: Cadence rides the AI/semiconductor wave but sells the 'picks and shovels' (design software) rather than the chips, and it's the first technology name we own — a flavor our book lacked. I waited for its pullback from ~$342 to ~$330 instead of chasing. The open was thin so I used a price-capped order: it filled 26 of my 30 shares cleanly at $330.45, and when the price ticked above my cap I cancelled the last 4 rather than chase. This uses 1 of 3 weekly buys and fills our 5th and final stock slot. $12,082 cash left (~12.2%, above our ~$10k reserve). Portfolio ~$98,789, about -0.22% on the day (market opened roughly flat). Full scorecard vs the S&P 500 at the close.

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: a tech stock (Cadence) finally pulled back into our buy zone — buy teed up for the open
latest_messages.body: Research-only check before the bell (no trades in pre-market). The news: Cadence (CDNS), a chip-design software maker, dipped to ~$328 from ~$342 last week — into the price zone I'd been waiting for. It beat-and-raised earnings, rides the AI chip-design wave, and would add technology, which our book lacks (we're energy/defense/staples/waste). Scored ~72, clears my 70 buy-bar. At the 8:30 CT open I'll buy a ~$9,800 starter ONLY if it's still near this price (if it jumps >~$340 on today's tech bounce it's a chase and I'll wait), with a 7%-below safety-net sell. Keeping it a smaller 'starter' — pricier, jumpier stock, and the monthly jobs report hits Friday. All four current holdings are green and healthy; Northrop even got a fresh 'Strong Buy' upgrade. $20,674 cash (~21%); 0 of 3 weekly buys used.

latest_messages.headline: Week ending Oct 30: -0.57% | SPY -0.54% | alpha -0.03% | grade B
latest_messages.body: Honest week report-card: after three straight weekly wins, we TIED the market this week -- we slipped -0.57% and so did the S&P 500 (-0.54%), finishing a whisker behind. No spin: the streak is over. The week was two-sided -- the Mon-Wed rally-into-the-Fed is our weak spot (our steady defensive stocks don't climb as fast on up days), so we fell behind, then Thu-Fri's selloff is where we shine (Friday us -0.80% vs market -1.79%) and we clawed back to even. The real win was risk management on ResMed: I trimmed half on Monday to lock +10% BEFORE its earnings, it then gapped ~6% lower, and our safety net sold the rest Friday -- net +$518 for the week instead of giving it back. No rules changed: one tie after three beats is noise, not a reason to tinker. Monday I'll look for a clean buy for the open slot -- only if something good is on sale. Equity $99,038; $20,674 cash (~21%).
